question: For the already identified Cosmos task3/init2 harmful first selection, do actual fixed-candidate 16-control future features restore the successful candidate ranking under the unchanged native Value scorer?
scope: Post-hoc mechanism diagnostic of the sole known harmful root. Not a new attack, independent replication, new episode success estimate, or reopening of the failed 30-root expansion gate.

findings.interpretation: This fixed realization supports local predicted-future sensitivity: changing only the Future text changes the Value ranking; replacing the future slots with encoded measured consequences restores the successful candidate ordering. Compared with the separately replayed actual futures, visual forecast error is higher under Swap for each candidate; the two branches share one root and are not independent task samples. These are separate measured facts, not a mediation percentage or a universal error-to-harm law.
findings.decision: Local causal explanation strengthened; keep this post-hoc countercheck bounded. No new attack/generalization claim and no reopening of the failed30-root expansion gate.
